questions.question: In computer architecture, what is the fundamental structural distinction between the classic Von Neumann architecture and the Harvard architecture?
options: Von Neumann architectures employ fixed-length instructions, whereas Harvard architectures rely exclusively on variable-length CISC instructions.
Von Neumann architectures execute instructions out-of-order, whereas Harvard architectures require strict in-order execution.

Von Neumann architectures utilize a single shared physical memory and bus system for both instructions and data, whereas Harvard architectures physically separate instruction and data memories and pathways.
Von Neumann architectures store operands exclusively in high-speed hardware registers, whereas Harvard architectures stream operands directly from main storage.
Von Neumann architectures implement hardware-managed floating-point coprocessors, whereas Harvard architectures handle floating-point calculations via software emulation.

questions.question: In multi-clock domain digital design, why are the read and write pointers of an asynchronous FIFO converted to Gray code before being passed through multi-flip-flop synchronizers across clock domains?
options: To guarantee that only a single bit changes between consecutive pointer increments, preventing multi-bit transition skews from causing the synchronizer to capture invalid intermediate pointer states.
To compress the pointer bit-width by half, thereby minimizing the silicon area required for the synchronization flip-flops and bus routing.
To eliminate setup and hold time requirements on the receiving synchronizer flip-flops through self-timed asynchronous handshaking.
To convert the cyclic binary counter values into linear arithmetic values, simplifying the generation of the FIFO 'full' and 'empty' comparison flags.
To reduce the switching frequency of the most significant bit (MSB), thereby lowering total dynamic power dissipation on the clock tree.

questions.question: In modern out-of-order superscalar processors, how does the Reorder Buffer (ROB) ensure that the processor maintains precise architectural exceptions despite speculative and out-of-order execution?
options: By stalling the instruction fetch and decode units immediately whenever any arithmetic instruction raises an internal execution fault in the execution stage.
By dynamically squashing instructions inside the reservation stations as soon as an execution pipeline reports an exception flag.
By checkpointing the complete physical register file into non-volatile shadow registers on every speculative branch instruction.
By executing faulting instructions twice sequentially to verify whether an exception is persistent or merely caused by transient soft errors.

By tracking speculative instruction state and strictly committing architectural results in original program order from the head of the buffer, deferring exception handling until the faulting instruction reaches the retirement head.

questions.question: In deep-submicron VLSI physical design and reliability engineering, what physical mechanism causes electromigration in on-chip metal interconnects, as governed by Black's equation?
options: Dielectric breakdown of the inter-metal dielectric (IMD) layer caused by high electric fields exceeding the critical oxide breakdown voltage.
Directional mass transport of metal conductor atoms caused by momentum transfer from conducting electrons ('electron wind'), leading to voids upstream and hillocks downstream.
Diffusion of substrate dopant impurities into lower metal layers driven by high thermal gradients between active devices and heat sinks.
Mechanical fracture of copper wires resulting from mismatched thermal expansion coefficients (CTE) between the silicon substrate and the packaging substrate.
Trapping of hot holes in the gate oxide interface during high-frequency switching, leading to a permanent shift in transistor threshold voltage.

questions.question: In high-performance computer architecture, what is the primary architectural advantage of a vector architecture that utilizes a dynamically configurable Vector Length Register (such as the RISC-V Vector extension or classic Cray vector processors) compared to a fixed-width packed SIMD architecture (such as x86 AVX-512)?
options: It guarantees deterministic single-cycle execution latency for all transcendental and matrix multiply instructions across all implementations.
It eliminates the requirement for data alignment or memory bank interleaving in the underlying cache and memory hierarchy.
It allows vector execution units to run at double the clock frequency of the scalar pipeline by pipeline-folding the arithmetic logic units.

It achieves Vector-Length Agnostic (VLA) binary compatibility, allowing the same compiled binary to scale efficiently across microarchitectures with different hardware vector register widths without code recompilation or complex loop-tail peeling.
It replaces all explicit vector register allocations with dynamic stack-based execution, eliminating register pressure entirely.
